evidence_quotes.quote: survey data of 652 randomly selected rural households from the Upper Ewaso
The Kenyan water policy framework recognizes WRUAs as the legal, grassroots collective action
The ESP model simultaneously models the membership to WRUA and the outcome
Holding a title deed had a positive influence on WRUA membership.
8%, income poor by about 47%, subjective poor by about 20% and water poor by about 14%.

country.comment: The study was conducted in the Upper Ewaso Ng'iro North Catchment Area in Kenya.
country.where_found: PDF p. 1, Title; PDF p. 2, Abstract; PDF p. 5, Section 2.1

effect_estimate.comment: Across all three treatment-effect estimators, collective-action participation via WRUA membership significantly reduced binary household water poverty (constructed from a polychoric PCA Water Poverty Index using a 40th-percentile cut-off), while holding a land title deed significantly predicted WRUA membership in the first stage but not water poverty directly in the second stage. Note that Table 7 prints *** on the ESP water-poverty ATT (-0.140, SE = 0.071) and ATU (-0.109, SE = 0.066) despite z-ratios of -1.97 and -1.65.
effect_estimate.value: Membership in legally recognized Water Resource Users Associations (WRUAs; N = 652 households: 331 members, 321 non-members) significantly reduced the probability of household water poverty: Endogenous Switching Probit (ESP) ATT = -0.140 (SE = 0.071, reported p < 0.01) and ATU = -0.109 (SE = 0.066, reported p < 0.01); Propensity Score Matching (4-nearest neighbors) ATT = -0.323 (SE = 0.044, p < 0.01); Inverse Probability Weighting ATT = -0.303 (SE = 0.038, p < 0.01). Descriptively, 23.36% of WRUA members vs. 52.34% of non-members were water poor (difference = 0.291, t = 8.021, p < 0.01), and 82.8% of WRUA members vs. 21.5% of non-members had piped water in their compound (difference = -0.613, t = -19.812, p < 0.01; domestic water collection time 3.299 vs. 20.436 minutes, t = 12.038, p < 0.01; traditional latrine without roof 6.0% vs. 10.6%, t = 2.111, p < 0.05). Holding a land title deed positively predicted WRUA membership in the first-stage probit (coeff. = 0.405, SE = 0.139, p < 0.01), had no statistically significant direct effect on water poverty in second-stage ESP regressions (coeff. = 0.160, SE = 0.188 for members; coeff. = 0.100, SE = 0.168 for non-members), and reduced non-members' income poverty (coeff. = -0.511, SE = 0.263, p < 0.05) and subjective poverty (coeff. = -0.382, SE = 0.179, p < 0.05). WRUA membership also reduced consumption poverty (ESP ATT = -0.084, SE = 0.006, p < 0.01), income poverty (ESP ATT = -0.472, SE = 0.012, p < 0.01), and subjective poverty (ESP ATT = -0.197, SE = 0.008, p < 0.01).
effect_estimate.where_found: PDF pp. 10-12, Tables 2, 3, and 5; PDF pp. 14-17, Section 3.3, Tables 6 and 7

mechanism_certainty.comment: Although appraised with ROBINS-I because the authors use endogenous switching IV/selection and PSM/IPW treatment-effect estimators, the study relies on cross-sectional observational survey data with Serious/Critical risk of bias (notably exclusion-restriction violations where selection instruments such as water conflict and river/borehole water sources directly overlap with components of the Water Poverty Index in Table A2, plus self-selection into WRUAs) and documents statistical associations rather than directly observing administrative or legal processes. Under CODEBOOK.md §9, certainty cannot exceed 2 and is coded 1 (documented statistical association).
